name: Poor Man's Covered Put (PMCP)
summary: Buy a deep-ITM long-dated put as a short-stock surrogate and sell a shorter-dated OTM put against it; the bearish mirror of the PMCC.

legs.strike_rule: Deep ITM by delta |0.80-0.90| (high strike). Extrinsic <= 10% of premium; never below |0.70| delta.
OTM by delta |0.20-0.30| (lower strike). HARD CONSTRAINT: long strike - short strike >= net debit per share.

max_profit: At or below the short strike at front expiry: approximately (long strike - short strike) x 100 - net debit + cumulative credits collected.
max_loss: The net debit less all credits collected, if the underlying rallies and the long put decays toward zero.
breakevens: Approximately long strike - net debit per share at the long's expiry; lower over time as credits accumulate.

greeks.vega: net positive - the long-dated put dominates; a vol crush hurts, which is a real headwind because vol usually FALLS as the market rallies and RISES as it falls (so vega and delta work together here, unlike the PMCC)

when_to_use: Bearish 6-18 month view on a broken underlying (spot < 50-day SMA < 200-day SMA), entered when IV rank is LOW (< 30) so the long put is not bought after a vol spike. Structurally harder than the PMCC because put skew makes the deep-ITM long put expensive and the OTM short put cheap - the financing ratio is worse. Verify the credit actually covers a meaningful fraction of the long's decay before trading it.
entry_rules: Trend filter: spot < 50-day SMA AND 50-day SMA < 200-day SMA.
IV rank < 30 at the time of the long put purchase (do not buy vega after a spike).
Long put delta |0.80-0.90|, DTE >= 180; extrinsic <= 10% of premium.
MANDATORY: long strike - short strike >= net debit per share.
Financing check: the front-month credit must be >= 3% of the net debit; if put skew makes that impossible, reject the trade.
Net debit <= 5% of equity per unit; maximum 3 concurrent PMCPs.
LEVEL 3 OK: a short put at a LOWER strike with an EARLIER expiry is covered by the long put. Submit as a 2-leg mleg; BUY THE LONG PUT FIRST if legging.
management_rules: Close the short put at 50-75% of the credit received and sell the next 21-45 DTE cycle at delta |0.20-0.30|.
If the short put's |delta| exceeds 0.50, roll down and out for a NET CREDIT only, keeping long strike - short strike >= remaining net debit.
Roll the long put forward when its |delta| drops below 0.70 or DTE < 120.
Hard stop: close everything if the long put's mark falls to 50% of purchase price, or if spot closes above the 200-day SMA for 3 consecutive sessions.
Track the running net debit (original debit minus cumulative credits) and reference it in every strike constraint.
Never sell more short puts than long puts owned.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short put by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the short put immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close any short put whose extrinsic falls below $0.10 - deep-ITM short puts are exercised early to capture interest, and this risk grows with rates.
Do NOT exercise the long put to cover an assignment; sell the assigned shares in the market and keep the long put's time value.
Close the long put no later than 90 DTE, and only after the short has been bought back.
Full exit: buy back the short put first, then sell the long put.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month put. Assignment delivers +100 shares at the short strike, requiring strike x 100 of buying power, hedged by a long higher-strike put. This is a cash-heavy event on a $50k account - a single $400 underlying assignment consumes $40,000. Size accordingly: cap the short strike x 100 at 40% of equity per position.
buying_power: Net debit only while both legs are open, because the long put at a higher strike and later expiry covers the short. An assignment temporarily consumes short strike x 100 of buying power until the shares are sold.
liquidity_needs: Long-dated deep-ITM puts are thin. OI >= 100 at the long strike, bid-ask <= 6% of mid. Restrict to SPY, QQQ, IWM and the most liquid single names.
common_mistakes: Ignoring put skew - the financing math is materially worse than the PMCC and many candidates do not clear the 3% credit test; buying the long put after a crash (max vega, max price); being assigned on a high-priced underlying and blowing through buying power; exercising the long put to cover instead of trading the shares.
zero_dte_notes: Never at 0DTE; minimum short DTE 21 at entry, forced close by 14:30 ET on expiry day.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
